title: new_with_signer_discovery: _cert_to_check parameter is unused, locks API to a no-op arg
description:
Trigger: every call to CrlChecker::new_with_signer_discovery (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:325-358).

The `cert_to_check: &Certificate` parameter is declared in the public signature (currently spelled `_cert_to_check` to silence the unused-variable lint) and the rustdoc (lines 281-288) explicitly says: 'It is taken at construction time only for ergonomic symmetry with the discovery flow; the actual revocation lookup happens at check_revocation call time. Passing a different cert argument to check_revocation later is well-defined.'

This is API surface that has zero behavioral effect today. Two consequences for the maintainer:

1. Future-self forgetting: in 12 months, a caller will rely on the parameter (perhaps believing it pre-validates the CRL covers cert_to_check) and the code will silently ignore it. They will file an issue about 'why doesn't new_with_signer_discovery reject when I pass the wrong cert.'

2. Post-1.0 lock-in: the parameter is part of the function signature. Removing it post-1.0 is a breaking change. Adding behavior to it post-1.0 is a behavior change that prior callers (who pass any cert) may have relied on as a no-op.

Per AGENTS.md 'design for the eventual complete shape' and 'breaking changes are free pre-1.0': decide now.

Options:
1. Remove the parameter entirely. Update the rustdoc to drop the 'ergonomic symmetry' rationale.
2. Make it meaningful: at construction time, check that the CRL is at least syntactically applicable to cert_to_check (e.g., issuer-DN match between cert.issuer and the discovered signer's subject, or run check_idp_dp_scope to fail-fast on out-of-scope CRLs before the caller even calls check_revocation).

Either is fine; the status quo (parameter present, behavior absent, doc explains it's pointless) is the worst of both worlds.
notes:
Analysis 2026-11-25: confirmed dead, and worse than dead -- but removing it is a breaking change to a published crate, so it needs your call on the version.

Confirmed: new_with_signer_discovery takes _cert_to_check: &Certificate (crl.rs:419) and never reads it. The constructor only needs bundle + crl, since discover_crl_signer(bundle, &crl) is the whole of discovery.

The bead calls it a no-op arg. It is actually worse than inert: it is misleading. check_revocation(cert, issuer) takes the certificate again at call time, and NOTHING ties that cert to the one named at construction. So the signature implies the checker is bound to a particular certificate when it is not -- you can construct with cert A and then check cert B. Any future use of the constructor parameter for validation would be unsound for exactly that reason, which rules out the other obvious fix of "just use it".

So the right fix is removal, not wiring it up.

Why I did not do it: pkix-revocation is 0.4.0 and f55d08e7 ("release: version bumps and changelogs for the Nov 2026 wave") released it, so dropping a public parameter is a 0.5.0 decision with a downstream effect on pkix-chain. That is a release call, not a cleanup.

When you take it: the only callers are in-repo tests (pkix-revocation/tests/pkits_4_5.rs, 6 call sites, plus crl_signer_revocation.rs). Mechanical change.

Related: PKIX-lnnl.6 is now closed. It concerned the same constructor and I had expected the unused parameter to be the missing input for that check -- it was not. The cert.issuer == CRL.issuer comparison happens in check_revocation, where the certificate is already available, so lnnl.6 was fixed without needing this parameter at all. That removes the last argument for keeping it.
close_reason:
Fixed, per your ruling to cut one breaking release. The parameter is gone.

Confirmed dead before removing: discovery uses only discover_crl_signer(bundle, &crl), so the certificate was never read.

Worse than inert, which is why wiring it up was not the alternative: check_revocation takes the certificate again at call time, and nothing tied the two together. A checker could be constructed naming certificate A and then used to check certificate B with no complaint. Any future use of the constructor argument for validation would therefore be unsound -- it would validate against a certificate the checker is not bound to. The rustdoc called it "ergonomic symmetry with the discovery flow", which is exactly the misleading framing: a constructor parameter implies a binding, and there was none.

Call sites updated: 13 in all. Worth noting three of them passed a certificate that existed for NO other purpose -- two test bindings in pkits_4_5.rs (both constructor-only negative tests) and the `leaf` binding in crl_signer_revocation.rs -- so the compiler flagged them as unused once the parameter went. That is independent evidence the argument was dead rather than merely unread.

One process note: my first enumeration of call sites was piped through `head` and hid the pkix-difftest caller (pkix-difftest/src/oracles/pkix_path.rs:348), which then failed the build. Enumerating call sites is not a place to truncate output.

Rustdoc rewritten to say the checker is not bound to a particular certificate, and to record what the old parameter implied, so nobody adds it back for symmetry.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2358 tests.
